The rule for D3b's per-room table in notes-D3.md (stage section 5; QD3-009 (3); logged before the table is built). One row for each of the 705 rooms, built by _analysis/d3b_room_table.py from the ledgers, never typed. Columns: the room; its batch (first batch, or pending, second batch, with the reason for each of the 10 reissued rooms: nine cut off mid-room, traaaaaaannnnnnnnnns to have its end marker repaired); why it was re-checked (recheck-scope.json: the rewritten, bounded, standing or entered elements its first return relied on, or a contrasting case); its verdict before (my D3a-56 ruling where the readers split, else the readers' agreed verdict, with their model version) and after (the re-check readers', agreed or split, with their version); the labelers' local status; its re-check lines by last ruling (shared: specifications and elaborations; corrections; limits, accepted with kind none; particulars; rejected; pending); and what the evidence pointed at in the room and what the re-check shows. Evidence that pointed at the rewrite in a room is (a) a D3a accepted correction on an element, and (b) a D3a-55 propose line accepted for a candidate. (a) is fixed where none of the room's re-check lines on that element is an accepted correction, and stands where one is. (b) is named where the room's re-check has an accepted line on that candidate, not absent, of kind specification, elaboration or correction, or a propose line held by it; otherwise not named. A re-check correction on an element where D3a accepted none in the room is new, and held (G61 (4)). A room with neither (a) nor (b) had nothing that pointed at the rewrite; its re-check tests the revised model. The re-check verdicts are reported and not ruled in this leg: their 160 splits are ruled when the second batch is back, over the full set with one criterion (section 4), and the readers' lines stand meanwhile, each with its version.
